sections.label: Singapore acceding to Montreal Protocol
sections.summary: Singapore will accede to the Montreal Protocol 2014, and the Tokyo Convention (Amendment) Bill will give effect to its provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Also, as a responsible member of the international civil aviation community, Singapore must do its part to address unruly passenger incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: That is why the Government will accede to the Protocol to Amend the Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft, also called the Montreal Protocol 2014 to the Tokyo Convention 1963.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Tokyo Convention (Amendment) Bill will give effect to the provisions of the Montreal Protocol 2014 and strengthen Singapore's ability to address unruly behaviour on board an aircraft.

sections.label: Aircraft commander restraint powers
sections.summary: Clause 6 empowers an aircraft commander to restrain an unruly passenger on reasonable grounds that a serious offence was committed on board.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 6 empowers the commander of an aircraft to take certain actions, such as restraining an unruly passenger, if the commander has reasonable grounds to believe that a serious offence has been committed on board the aircraft.

sections.label: Action limited to Singapore carriers
sections.summary: Current practice and guidelines let Singapore act only if persons arrive on a Singapore Airlines plane or other Singapore carriers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the current practice and guidelines, Singapore can only take action if the person or persons arrive on a Singapore Airlines (SIA) plane or other Singapore carriers.

sections.label: Tokyo Convention updated by Montreal Protocol
sections.summary: The Tokyo Convention 1963 was updated through the Montreal Protocol signed on 4 April 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Tokyo Convention 1963 was updated through the Montreal Protocol signed on 4 April 2014.

sections.label: Where punishment will be served
sections.summary: The question asks whether punishment under the new Act is served in the passenger's own country or the country where the aircraft landed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Fifth, will the sentence or punishment with the new Act be served in the passenger's own country or the country where the aircraft landed, or where the aircraft is at, that is, the state of the country of offence or the country of registration?

sections.label: Support for Montreal Protocol provisions
sections.summary: The speaker supports adopting the Montreal Protocol 2014 provisions giving Singapore jurisdiction as state of landing or operator to punish unruly passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Having good and enforceable laws, as well as solid enforcement procedures, in this respect may also assist in dealing with, or preventing disruptions by passengers with terrorism-related intentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support the adoption of the provisions to the Montreal Protocol of 2014 giving Singapore the jurisdiction as a state of landing or the state of the operator to take punitive action against unruly passengers who may have committed offences against penal law or carried out acts which may jeopardise the safety of an aircraft or of persons or property in such aircraft, or which jeopardise good order and discipline on board.

sections.label: Conflict between commander and marshal
sections.summary: The new provisions may create conflict, possibly leading the aircraft commander and air marshal to act independently without coordination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The above-mentioned new provisions may well give rise to an element of conflict leading possibly to both the aircraft commander and the air marshal taking independent actions without coordination.

sections.label: Adequacy of laws for ICAO offences
sections.summary: The Member asks whether existing laws and the Bill's amendments cover all offences in ICAO Circular 288.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, I would also like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether our existing laws, together with the proposed amendments and inclusions under this Bill, are adequate to include all offences listed in the International Civil Aviation Organisation's (ICAO's) Circular 288?

sections.label: Unruly passenger incidents reported
sections.summary: Over 58,000 unruly passenger incidents were reported on aircraft in flight between 2007 and 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Over 58,000 unruly passenger incidents were reported on aircraft in flight between 2007 and 2016.

sections.label: Definition of unruly passenger
sections.summary: The Member asks whether there is a clear definition of an unruly passenger and what triggers enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, is there a clear definition of an unruly passenger and what must he or she do for enforcement actions to be taken against him or her?

sections.label: Common airline database proposal
sections.summary: The Member asks whether aviation authorities would consider a common airline database centralising details of recalcitrant unruly passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the aviation authorities consider working together to establish a common database among airlines to centralise details of recalcitrant unruly passengers?

sections.label: Unruly cases and Montreal Protocol 2014
sections.summary: Fewer than 10 cases a year occurred over five years, many on SIA Group aircraft, and Montreal Protocol 2014 will enhance Singapore's handling of unruly incidents on non-Singapore controlled aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Based on the information that I have, there are, on average, about less than 10 cases per year over the last five years, and many of these took place on SIA Group aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The Montreal Protocol 2014 will enhance Singapore’s ability to handle unruly incidents on board a non-Singapore controlled aircraft.

sections.label: Bill grants enforcement powers
sections.summary: The Bill will give Singapore legal capacity to exercise enforcement powers and take necessary action in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The Bill will enable Singapore to have the relevant legal capacity to exercise enforcement powers and take the necessary action as warranted in such cases.

sections.label: Aircraft commander restraint powers
sections.summary: The aircraft commander can impose measures including restraint on an unruly passenger and get help from cabin crew, passengers or air marshals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The aircraft commander can impose measures, including restraint, on an unruly passenger and obtain the assistance of the cabin crew, passengers or air marshals.

sections.label: India No-Fly List monitoring
sections.summary: India's 2017 No-Fly List bans unruly passengers from three months to life; Singapore monitors such lists and will assess feasibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For example, India introduced a national No-Fly List in 2017, which identifies unruly passengers and prohibits them from boarding flights.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Depending on the seriousness of the offence, the flight ban on the passenger ranges from three months to a possible life ban.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We are currently monitoring the development of such No-Fly Lists by the other countries and will assess if it is feasible to introduce and address some of our context in Singapore.

sections.label: Jurisdiction, Circular 288, air marshals
sections.summary: Existing procedures cover multi-state jurisdiction; similar offences exist and are reviewed; in conflict, the aircraft commander takes control over air marshals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to the last question, there are existing procedures between and among states concerning the exercise of jurisdiction where more than one has jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As to Circular 288, currently, we do have similar offences in our legislation but we do review them regularly and, if necessary, we can also include some of them where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to the role of the air marshal as well as the aircraft commander, the air marshals are deployed in the aircraft for a certain reason, and they have very strict rules of engagement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: However, should there be a conflict, the commander of the aircraft will take control because he is, ultimately, the overall in-charge of the aircraft.
